clue.text: Sign on back of door by itself turned back round

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter, so only the tail end is wanted
something turned back faces the other way, so read the word from right to left
going round something means surrounding it, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: alone, on its own
the final letter of door

explanation.surface: A notice on the back of a door has flipped itself around.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversed word for 'by itself' wraps round the last letter of door.
explanation.definitionFit: To enrol is to register or put your name down, which is what signing on means.

clue.text: What one gets for a pound?

definitions.text: What one gets for a pound?

blocks.clueFragment: What one gets for a pound?
blocks.note: surface reading: what a pound coin buys you in a shop
setter's reading: the amount of foreign currency handed over in return for sterling

explanation.walkthrough: The question sounds like shopping; it is about changing money at the bureau before a holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: The figure at a currency counter states how many euros or dollars are given per unit of sterling.

clue.text: Clear, when blood type checked, so not this?

definitions.text: Clear, when blood type checked, so not this?

indicators.note: something checked is held back or contained, so these letters are enclosed

blocks.note: to rid is to clear away
AB is one of the blood groups

explanation.surface: A patient whose blood test comes back clear is therefore free of infection.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: after a clean blood test, you are not suffering from rabies.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabid means infected with rabies, which a clear blood test would rule out.

clue.text: Does he have the property of crippling networks?

definitions.text: Does he have the property of crippling networks?

blocks.note: surface reading: someone who holds real estate
setter's reading: something that knocks out local area networks, a computer saboteur

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as LAN DOWNER: a LAN is a local area network, and a downer brings it down.
explanation.definitionFit: An owner of estates holds real property, and the split form describes something that takes local computer links offline.

clue.text: Shopping centre not entirely prepared for poet

indicators.note: not the entire word, so its final letter is dropped

blocks.note: a mall is a shopping centre
armed and ready, prepared for a fight

explanation.surface: A shopping mall is only half ready for a visiting poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Stéphane Mallarmé was a French Symbolist poet of the nineteenth century.

clue.text: One on hand is always sober in appearance

indicators.note: one thing sitting in another, so the first is enclosed by the second

blocks.note: mien is a person's look or bearing
TT, teetotal, never drinking alcohol

explanation.surface: A person always on call looks permanently sober.
explanation.definitionFit: A mitten is a glove without separate fingers, something worn on the hand.

clue.text: Double up, needing a half-dose of painkiller — this?

definitions.text: Double up, needing a half-dose of painkiller — this?

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means reading from the bottom, so the word runs backwards
only half the dose is given, so just the first half of the word is kept

blocks.note: dual means double, twofold
taken as written
something that numbs, read literally

explanation.surface: Someone doubled over in pain needs a smaller dose of their medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also points at the answer: a historic opiate painkiller that someone in agony would take.
explanation.definitionFit: Laudanum was a tincture of opium widely used as a painkiller in Victorian times.

clue.text: Range of old invaders, heading to the centre

indicators.note: the head of the word is moved to its middle, so it is placed inside what is left

blocks.note: the Danes raided and settled in England in the Viking age

explanation.surface: A band of ancient raiders marches towards the middle of the country.
explanation.walkthrough: The first letter of the invaders moves into the middle of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: The Andes are the mountain range running down western South America.

clue.text: Tinker’s despairing admission, becoming beggar

blocks.note: to tinker with is to try to repair
a cry of defeat: I can't

explanation.surface: A travelling tinker admits failure and ends up begging.
explanation.walkthrough: A tinker was an itinerant mender of pots, and the clue has one trying to repair something then giving up.
explanation.definitionFit: A mendicant lives by asking for alms, as with the mendicant friars.

clue.text: Sweet, but one contributes little to high-level debate?

definitions.text: one contributes little to high-level debate?

blocks.note: first meaning: a dessert, a steamed sponge with dried fruit

blocks.clueFragment: one contributes little to high-level debate?
blocks.note: second, whimsical meaning: a stodgy, silent member of a government's top table

explanation.walkthrough: The second half reads the name literally: a pudding in the sense of a dull lump who sits in the Cabinet without speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a traditional British steamed dessert, and pudding is also slang for a dull, heavy person sitting among ministers.

clue.text: New, really honest column in paper

indicators.note: something new is made afresh, so the letters are reworked

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A newspaper's latest column is truly candid.
explanation.walkthrough: The section where single people advertise for partners is famously not always really honest.
explanation.definitionFit: A lonely hearts column is the personal advertisement section of a newspaper where people seek partners.

clue.text: Damsel in distress wants an Arabian to carry her, finally rejecting a couple

indicators.note: rejecting a couple of letters at the end means the last two are thrown away

blocks.note: taken as written
the one-humped Arabian camel, a beast to ride on

explanation.surface: A distressed young woman needs a desert camel to carry her away to safety.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Andromeda was chained to a rock for a sea monster until Perseus rescued her, the classic maiden in peril.

clue.text: County’s old pupils have no heart to return

indicators.note: losing the heart means the central letter is taken out
returning means going back the way you came, so read right to left

blocks.note: O is the standard abbreviation for old
schoolgirls are pupils

explanation.surface: Former pupils of a county school have lost the heart to go back.
explanation.walkthrough: Old girls is the phrase for former pupils; the five-letter word loses its middle R before the whole lot is turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Sligo is a county on the north-west coast of Ireland.

clue.text: Hunger unduly to comprehend item of grammar

indicators.note: to comprehend is to take in, so the answer is held inside the words

blocks.note: found across the two words

explanation.surface: Someone craving food excessively is trying to understand a point of grammar.
explanation.definitionFit: A gerund is a verb form ending -ing used as a noun, a standard grammatical term.

clue.text: Able to recover soldiers I infiltrated without noise

indicators.note: to infiltrate is to slip inside, so one piece goes into the other

blocks.note: RE, the Royal Engineers
making no sound
taken as written

explanation.surface: A soldier recovers after silently slipping behind enemy lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Resilient people or materials bounce back from strain or setbacks.

clue.text: In contract, check having a firm grasp

indicators.note: placed in something means sitting inside it, so the other words go within

blocks.note: to purse the lips is to contract them
CH is the chess abbreviation for check
taken as written

explanation.surface: A contract is checked by someone with a firm grip on the details.
explanation.definitionFit: Purchase means a hold or leverage that stops slipping, as in getting purchase on a rock face.

clue.text: Angry snake: it may force you out of your way

definitions.text: it may force you out of your way

blocks.note: cross means annoyed
to snake is to wind, as a road does

explanation.surface: An angry serpent might drive you off the path.
explanation.walkthrough: Snake is the verb, not the reptile.
explanation.definitionFit: A crosswind blows across your path of travel and can push a car, plane or cyclist off course.

clue.text: In chair, one has not to name coastal area

indicators.note: a thing that has something holds it within, so the following words go inside

blocks.note: a chair is a seat
as in to and fro, the opposite direction of to
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: Someone in the chair has been told not to name a seaside spot.
explanation.walkthrough: The pairing to and fro lets 'not to' mean its partner word.
explanation.definitionFit: A seafront is the part of a seaside town along the shore, with its promenade and beach.

clue.text: Taken to be a lackey, wearing scarlet

indicators.note: something worn is put on around you, so one piece is clothed in the other

blocks.note: scarlet is a shade of red
a lackey's job is to wait on others

explanation.surface: A footman in scarlet livery is hired to be someone's servant.
explanation.definitionFit: A reserved seat or table is one already booked, so it is taken.

clue.text: Piano regularly positioned in arch

indicators.note: placed inside another word, so that word surrounds this one

blocks.note: arch means knowingly mischievous
often, frequently

explanation.surface: A piano is placed at regular points within an archway.
explanation.walkthrough: Piano here is the musical direction, not the instrument; arch is the adjective meaning cunning.
explanation.definitionFit: Piano is the Italian musical marking telling the player to perform quietly.

clue.text: I agree small rise for royal minister

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means reading upwards, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: an expression of agreement
low as in a small amount

explanation.surface: A minister to the crown accepts a modest pay rise.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardinal Thomas Wolsey was Lord Chancellor and chief minister to Henry VIII.

clue.text: Note Roman law’s old-fashioned message

blocks.note: te is a note of the sol-fa scale
lex is Latin for law

explanation.surface: Remember that Roman law is now outdated communication.
explanation.definitionFit: A telex was a printed message sent over a teleprinter network, superseded by fax and email.

clue.text: Clicking tongue has ox on the move

indicators.note: things on the move change position, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A tongue clicking at an ox to drive it along.
explanation.walkthrough: Tongue means language here, not the body part.
explanation.definitionFit: Xhosa is a South African language famous for its click consonants.

clue.text: Cheats in marriage — disaster in a couple of moves

definitions.text: disaster in a couple of moves

blocks.note: fools means tricks or deceives
a spouse, one of the partners in a marriage

explanation.surface: Infidelity in a marriage leads to disaster almost at once.
explanation.definitionFit: Fool's mate is the fastest possible checkmate in chess, delivered by Black on the second move, a humiliating rout.

clue.text: Pupil with a small swelling losing one mark

indicators.note: losing something means it is taken away, so these letters go

blocks.note: taken as written
a spot on the skin
Roman numeral one
M for the German mark currency

explanation.surface: A schoolchild with a spot loses a mark in the test.
explanation.walkthrough: Pupil is the eye, not the schoolchild: the apple of the eye was an old name for the pupil.
explanation.definitionFit: The apple of the eye originally meant the pupil, thought to be a solid round ball.

clue.text: Great admirer of man keeping quiet in argument over killer

indicators.note: something keeping a thing holds it, so the surrounding words enclose it

blocks.note: he, a male person
a row is a quarrel
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over
a ripper is a murderer, as in Jack the Ripper
sh is the call for silence

explanation.surface: A devoted fan of a man stays silent through a row about a murderer.
explanation.walkthrough: The hush sits inside the killer, just after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A hero-worshipper idolises someone, admiring them to excess.

clue.text: Secret way to get fit, avoiding hospital at first

indicators.note: avoiding something means leaving it out, so a letter is dropped

blocks.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
fit and well
H is the map abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A hidden method of getting fit that keeps you out of hospital in the first place.
explanation.walkthrough: The H removed is the first letter of the fit word, which is why the clue says at first.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealthy actions are done quietly and covertly, so they are secret.

clue.text: Medical men say arrested? They weren’t drunk

indicators.note: a person arrested is held, so these doctors hold the next word

blocks.note: Drs is the abbreviation for doctors
eg, for example

explanation.surface: Doctors claim someone was detained, but insist they were sober.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads like a defence of drivers; it means the bits left in the glass that nobody drank.
explanation.definitionFit: Dregs are the sediment left at the bottom of a cup or bottle, the part that remains undrunk.
